findings.title: Negative-offset slicing on Django QuerySet always raises, contradicting the advertised feature
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start_offset. Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ explicitly rejects negative start/stop values in slices (it raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`), so this code path cannot work as described. The accompanying comment claims 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' which is factually incorrect. As soon as a client supplies a negative cursor offset with `enable_advanced_features=True` (reachable from OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint via `optimized_pagination=true`), the request will raise an unhandled exception (500) instead of the intended 'advanced pagination'.

findings.title: Potential AttributeError when organization_context.member is None
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` will evaluate `organization_context.member.has_global_access` whenever the requesting user is not a superuser. If `organization_context.member` can be None (e.g., edge cases where a user has org access without a direct member record, which RpcUserOrganizationContext explicitly supports as an optional field), this raises an AttributeError and turns a valid, permitted request into an unhandled 500 error.

findings.title: Unrelated, under-specified feature introduced in a PR about spans buffer
findings.body: This endpoint change (adding an `optimized_pagination` query parameter that swaps in OptimizedCursorPaginator with 'advanced features' for superusers/global-access members) is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose ('Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert'). It introduces new user-facing API behavior gated by a client-supplied flag with no validation of cursor offsets, no tests, and depends on the broken negative-offset handling in OptimizedCursorPaginator (see paginator.py finding). This should either be reverted from this PR or properly scoped, tested, and reviewed on its own merits.

findings.title: Redirect traversal depth silently reduced from 10000 to 1000 with explanatory comment removed
findings.body: The loop bound for following span-id redirects was lowered from `0, 10000` to `0, 1000`, and the comment that explained the implication of this limit ('theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly') was deleted entirely instead of being updated. This silently reduces the maximum depth of a span tree that can be correctly merged via redirects, and removes the only documentation of this known limitation, making it harder for future maintainers to understand why extremely deep traces might not merge correctly.

findings.title: max_segment_spans parameter is now dead/unenforced in Python, duplicating an inconsistent hardcoded cap in Lua
findings.body: `SpansBuffer.__init__` still accepts and stores `max_segment_spans: int = 1001`, but the corresponding enforcement code in `_load_segment_data` (which used to skip/log segments exceeding this span count) was removed in this PR. The only remaining cap on segment size is the hardcoded `1000` threshold inside `add-buffer.lua`'s `zpopmin` eviction logic, which is off-by-one from the Python-side `max_segment_spans=1001` and not configurable from Python anymore. This leaves a now-meaningless constructor parameter and removes a defense-in-depth check that previously protected the flush path if the Lua-side cap were ever bypassed (e.g., due to script version skew during a rolling deploy).

findings.title: No test coverage for the new eviction-on-insert behavior
findings.body: This PR's stated purpose is to add eviction during span insertion (capping a segment at 1000 spans via `zpopmin` in add-buffer.lua). None of the tests added or modified in this PR (test_buffer.py, test_consumer.py, test_flusher.py) exercise a scenario with more than 1000 spans in a single segment to verify that the oldest spans are correctly evicted and that `flush_segments`/`done_flush_segments` behave correctly on an evicted segment. The core feature being shipped is untested.

findings.title: Misleading comment added without any corresponding functional change
findings.body: A comment claiming 'Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios' was added above `self.offset = int(offset)`, but no actual behavior changed here (the line is identical to before). This creates the false impression that negative-offset support was added/validated at the Cursor level, when in fact no validation or handling of negative offsets exists anywhere in this class, and downstream consumers (e.g., Django querysets) do not support negative slicing at all.
